traceBase: Existing lifecycle trace DTOs: schemaVersion, fixtureID, engine, normalizationRules, identityMapping, operationMapping, initialCut, steps, oldReads, rawCounts, scope; FDB also finalRawCurrent. Step/observation/raw record encodings remain those of the accepted lifecycle exporter. Every step also includes OriginalRequest with the same exact source-produced request shape used by faults; this is needed for all six post-reopen retries.
unusedIdentity: life-a2 is a declared mapping only: it never appears in observed Lives or NewLives.
oldReadRule: Every Cut equals its original step Cut within the same engine. Reopened-at View equals original After. Held-old is the exact edge-only view including actual LifeRecord, observed before whole-cohort teardown and then closed; all reopened-at reads occur after whole-cohort reopen. Every old read adds Checkpoint (before-cohort-stop|after-cohort-reopen) and actual controller EventID. ABA value equality never replaces RevisionOperation/provenance equality.

faultRecord.Marker: Nonempty actual pause/failure boundary description; retained engine-specific evidence, not cross-engine numeric equality
faultRecord.CallerClassification: Exact case classification above; never inferred from later observer success

OriginalRequest.Payload: Base64 exact original source-produced input bytes
OriginalRequest.Graph: Own engine graph identity from identityMapping; all other request/result coordinates bind the associated operationMapping entry.

Observer.View: Complete lifecycle View at recovered operation
Observer.RawRecords: Actual durable original records for this operation

faultRecord.Intermediate: Only precommit case: {Classification: pending|old-complete, Raw: base64 actual read response, Cut/View/RawObservation only when old-complete}. Native pending is allowed; FDB old-complete is allowed and must equal seed After. No partial complete view is allowed.
faultRecord.Retry: First two cases only, AFTER recovery has resolved/observed the original commit: {RawResult: base64 actual recovered/retry response, Payload: base64 bytes exactly equal OriginalRequest.Payload, Result: {Coordinator,Request,Transaction,Round} exactly equal operationMapping, Before: observation, After: observation, NewRawRecords: actual new replay application records}. Observation is {Cut,View,RawObservation}; Before/After equal recovered step After semantically, and raw complete-group inventory does not grow. New native CDC must be empty. Original payload SHA256 is computed and reported by checker; emit InputSHA256 consistently if supplied.
faultRecord.ChangedPayload: Lost-reply case only: {Payload: base64 otherwise-valid changed source-produced input under original key, Classification: mismatch, Raw: base64 actual refusal, Before: observation, After: observation, NewRawRecords: actual new refusal application records}. Payload differs; Views AND actual raw complete-group inventories are unchanged and new native CDC is empty. FDB decoded input must pass fixed graph shape and retain ID/Request/Coordinator.
faultRecord.ProcessEvidence: Ordered actual controller events using global positive EventID, Action kill|stop|commit|reopen, Role client|replica|storage, Member (native voter1..6 or FDB server0..3; client label otherwise), Instance (actual process-instance identity), Volume (actual durable-volume identity or empty for client), Raw (base64 actual evidence). kill/stop events add Reaped=true, actual Signal (SIGKILL|SIGTERM|clean-exit), and OOMKilled (actual bool, or null where native OS does not expose it). reopen events add PreviousInstance, Ready=true and RecoveryRaw (actual startup/recovery observation); they DO NOT claim Reaped. Instance must change and Volume must match the stopped predecessor. commit events add Result {Coordinator,Request,Transaction,Round} and actual durable-record Raw; no caller success flag. Native opaque evidence stays exporter-qualified. Repeated references to one global event are permitted only when byte/field-identical.
faultRecord.CallerRaw: Base64 actual caller response/error or killed-call record supporting CallerClassification; a later observer receipt is not caller delivery.
faultRecord.ReopenRetries: Same-volume case only: exactly six entries ordered like operations, each {Operation, EventID, Payload, Result: {Coordinator,Request,Transaction,Round}, RawResult: base64 actual recovered/retry response, Before: observation, After: observation, NewRawRecords: actual new replay records}. EventIDs follow the final ready/recovery event. Payload equals its step OriginalRequest.Payload byte-for-byte. Result equals its own operationMapping entry; Before/After equal final step6 semantically and actual complete six-group/raw ledger inventory does not grow. No new native CDC. These execute recover/retry, not disk scan substitutes.

comparisonBoundary: Native opaque certificates/outcome codecs remain qualified by the actual exporter; Python does not decode them into authority. Raw source-qualified records are retained and simple graph/scope/index bindings checked. Compare semantic effects, original key/result identities, complete logical groups and historical revisions; never equate numeric engine rounds/cuts, physical transaction counts or Pending with an empty answer.
acceptanceLimit: Local functional paired comparison only: not multi-host, power loss, arbitrary failure schedules, cost/performance or engine selection. Existing scalar, graph-fault and lifecycle encodings remain unchanged; this is a fresh fixture namespace.

processRules.precommit-uncertainty: Actual client SIGKILL/reap after Marker boundary; caller remains unknown; observer later proves original committed result. Intermediate native pending or FDB old-complete is explicit.
processRules.lost-committed-reply: Actual pre-kill durable commit event precedes client SIGKILL/reap and caller receipt remains unknown. MarkerRaw and commit Raw contain actual outcome/decision bytes or the persisted original records captured BEFORE kill, linked to the same operation and later observer records; a ready-only marker plus later observation is insufficient.
processRules.quorum-preserving-failure: Exact replica/storage kill+reap event precedes commit event while that SAME instance remains down (no intervening reopen). Commit Result equals operationMapping and actual durable record is retained.
processRules.same-volume-reopen: Entire cohort: native members1..6, FDB members0..3, each with actual stop/kill+reap and a distinct ready replacement linked to SAME nonempty volume. Every cohort stop EventID precedes every cohort reopen EventID. Already-killed members may reference earlier byte-identical stop events. No client-only reopen substitutes storage recovery. Held-old EventID precedes first cohort stop; reopened-at EventIDs follow last cohort ready event. Actual stop signal/OOM status is preserved, never filled from expectations.

artifactRootValidation: FDB qualification requires explicit artifact root: all controllerArtifacts hashes, backendTraceArtifact hash and exact backend content after only specified controller additions, sealed controllerCommandLedger exact byte prefix of final commands.jsonl, and raw marker/process/recovery/retry fields independently linked to those files and ledger entries. Native transparent OS fields bind actual PID/member/incarnation/directory/wait status/startup bytes; opaque native authority remains exporter-qualified.
